predecessors.name: Kingdom of Portugal
predecessors.text: the Kingdom of Portugal and the Algarves with its colonies as the 1908-1910 Cliopatria shape draws them (Cliopatria's Kingdom shape lacks Goa and Timor, which the Republic's first shape adds)

predecessors.name: Portuguese Empire
predecessors.text: Goa and the other Indian enclaves and Portuguese Timor, which Cliopatria's Portuguese Colonies row draws to 1910 (24,277 km2) and the Republic's 1911 shape takes over

successors.name: Portugal (Estado Novo and Third Republic)
successors.text: the same metropole and colonies (7,574 cells, identical to the Republic's 1919-1925 shape) passing to the military dictatorship after the 28 May 1926 coup

ledger.x: 1910: the republican uprising of 5 October overthrows King Manuel II and Portugal becomes a republic.
1914: south-east Angola enters the Portuguese map.
1914: Germans take Naulila and the Humbe region.
1915: General Pereira d'Eca's column fights the Cuanhama.
10 April 1916: Portugal occupies the Kionga Triangle.
November 1917: Lettow-Vorbeck's German column enters Mozambique.
August 1918: the German column leaves Portuguese Mozambique.
1919: the Kionga Triangle is ceded to Portugal at Versailles.
28 May 1926: a coup d'etat by the armed forces ends the First Republic.

wars.name: Portugal in World War I
wars.outcome: Allied victory; Portugal seized German ships on 23-25 February 1916, Germany declared war on 9 March 1916 and Austria-Hungary on 15 March; the armistice was 11 November 1918.

wars.name: German-Portuguese clashes in southern Angola (Naulila)
wars.outcome: German attacks at Cuangar (31 October 1914) and Naulila (18 December 1914) drive the Portuguese from the Humbe region; Pereira d'Eca lands in March 1915, reoccupies Humbe on 7 July 1915 and the German force in South West Africa surrenders to Botha on 9 July.

wars.name: Cuanhama campaign of 1915
wars.outcome: Portuguese win: the Cuamato fort reoccupied 15 August, the Battle of Mongua 18-20 August, Ondjiva occupied without resistance on 4 September 1915; Mandume dies in 1917.

wars.name: Kionga Triangle occupation
wars.outcome: Portugal occupies the triangle on 10 April 1916; the Treaty of Versailles cedes Kionga to Portugal on 28 June 1919 (Portuguese Mozambique page).

wars.name: German invasion of Portuguese Mozambique
wars.outcome: Lettow-Vorbeck crosses into Mozambique on 23 November 1917, routs the garrison at Ngomano, lives off Portuguese supplies for nine months, takes Namacurra in July 1918 and returns to German East Africa in August 1918; no land changes owner.

wars.name: Barue uprising
wars.outcome: The page gives no result: 'Also in 1917, the Barue uprising took place and while it lasted, the Germans invaded Mozambique with 300 soldiers and 1,700 askari'.

wars.name: Portuguese campaigns of pacification and occupation, 1910-1915 phase
wars.outcome: Angola: Cassai reached and the north-east complete in 1912, the Cuanhama beaten in 1915, the south 'only pacified in 1926'.

certainty.note: Mainland Portugal and the colonies' treaty frontiers (the Angola page: the Barotseland frontier by the 1905 award of the King of Italy; borders with other powers fixed during the Scramble) are sharp on paper.

sources.title: Portuguese campaigns of pacification and occupation
